title: How to verify a business address
summary: An address on an application is a claim. How to check that it exists, work out what kind of place it is, and tell whether the business really operates there…
body_markdown:
Establish three things. Confirm that the address exists and is written correctly with postal data such as the USPS ZIP Code lookup or Royal Mail's postcode finder, then work out what kind of place it is from dated street imagery, a search of who else uses the address and the property record. Finally, check whether the business operates there, using the registry's address history, the business's website and listings, other people's reviews and records, and whether its phone number and shipping address tell the same story.


A registered office, or a registered agent's address in the US, is an address the register publishes for the company, and in the US the agent is the one who accepts legal papers for it. It can be an accountant's, a solicitor's or an agent's address. The business address, which some state forms call the principal office, is where the business says it is run from, and a business may trade from somewhere else again.


In the US, run it through the USPS ZIP Code lookup, which has a field showing whether the address is in USPS's table of Commercial Mail Receiving Agencies, the USPS term for a private business that rents private mailboxes, and can return a claimed suite number as a PMB, or private mailbox. That shows the address is a mailbox business and leaves open whether the box exists. Then search the address itself: a mailbox store or virtual office rents out its address, so a search can turn up the provider's own name and many other businesses giving the same street address with different suite numbers. Dated street imagery shows whether the building is a shopfront, an office block or a house.


Not on its own. Working from home is common: in 2025, 35 percent of employed people in the US did some or all of their work at home on days they worked, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Owners can also use an accountant's address, an agent or a mailbox to keep their home address off public records and parcels. It becomes a question when the address is the only trace of the business and contradicts what it says about where it operates.


In the US, look up the parcel in the county assessor's records, which can include the owner's name, the mailing address and a land use code, though some counties, such as Sacramento, do not show owner information online. In England and Wales, HM Land Registry's title register usually includes who owns the property and costs £7. The owner may be a landlord, so the record often tells you more about what kind of building it is than about who works inside.


Read its filings in date order. Companies House's filing history records each change of registered office with the old address, the new one and the date, and its free email alerts tell you when a company updates details such as its address. In California, the Statement of Information an LLC files every two years asks for its principal office and mailing address, and plain copies are free online.
